issues.detail: Hebrew has four sons: פִּיתוֹן (Pithon), וָמֶלֶךְ (Melech), וְתַאְרֵעַ (Tarea), וְאָחָז (Ahaz). Chinese renders '比他音' for Pithon (acceptable transliteration), '王' for Melech (Melech means 'king', but here it is a proper name, not a common noun; rendering as 王 loses the name), '他阿耳雅' for Tarea (acceptable), and '亞哈斯' for Ahaz (acceptable). The issue is that 'Melech' is translated as '王' (king) instead of being transliterated as a name, which changes the proper name into a common noun, causing a reader to miss that Melech is a personal name.
